title: Gurnoor Brar's 4 for 30 Bowls India to Four-Run DLS Win and 2-0 Series Lead
excerpt: New Zealand were bowled out for 134 in Wellington, their lowest home ODI total against India, before rain ended India's chase at 113 for 7 — four runs ahead of the DLS par score.
body:
• India beat New Zealand by four runs under the DLS method in Wellington to take a 2-0 lead in the five-match ODI series.
  • Gurnoor Brar took a career-best 4 for 30 and was player of the match as New Zealand were bowled out for 134 — their lowest home ODI total against India.
  • Brar's figures are the second-best by an Indian pacer in an ODI in New Zealand, behind Javagal Srinath's 4 for 23 in Auckland in 2003.
  • India's chase stalled at 113 for 7 in 26 overs, four runs ahead of the DLS par score of 109, when rain ended play. The third ODI is in Hamilton on Tuesday, November 10.

India's bowlers won a match their batters nearly threw away in Wellington on Saturday, beating New Zealand by four runs under the DLS method to go 2-0 up in the five-match ODI series. Gurnoor Brar, the young right-arm seamer, took a career-best 4 for 30 as New Zealand were dismissed for 134 in 41 overs — their lowest all-out total at home against India in one-day internationals, according to MyKhel's analysis of the match.

Rain had already cut the contest to 47 overs a side after a delayed start at Hnry Stadium. On a two-paced pitch offering movement, New Zealand never built an innings: Daryl Mitchell's 55 was the only substantial score, with Mitchell Santner adding 31.

Brar breaks the innings open

Brar did his damage in the middle overs. In the 20th over he struck twice — Tom Latham top-edged a pull and Glenn Phillips followed in the same over — to leave the hosts 53 for 5. He later removed Santner and Nathan Smith to finish with 4 for 30 from his 10 overs. Anshul Kamboj (2 for 25), Axar Patel (2 for 28) and Auqib Nabi (2 for 31) shared the remaining wickets.

According to MyKhel, Brar's spell is the second-best ODI bowling performance by an Indian pacer in New Zealand, behind only Javagal Srinath's 4 for 23 in Auckland in 2003. Across the first two matches of the series, India's seamers have taken nine wickets with short deliveries — five of them Brar's.

"Really enjoyed bowling here in NZ — the bounce and pace. In India, the pitches are flat and you have to bowl the hard length. Here there's more bounce. If you are a fast bowler bowling at 140-142 kph, you have to be aggressive, but you have to know your limits as well."

— Gurnoor Brar, Player of the Match

A chase that almost slipped away

Chasing a revised target, India lost Shubman Gill in the second over and kept losing wickets. Shreyas Iyer made 30 and KL Rahul an unbeaten 26, but Kyle Jamieson (3 for 35) and Jacob Duffy (3 for 35) dragged New Zealand back into the game. When rain stopped play, India were 113 for 7 after 26 overs — four runs ahead of the DLS par score of 109 — and the match was called off at the cut-off time.

Captain Shubman Gill praised his young pace attack, which is operating without Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj: "In the last match, Gurnoor bowled really well too. As he gets more experience, he'll get more consistent. He already has the pace and bounce," Gill said, according to ESPNcricinfo's match report.

What it means

India lead the series 2-0 and can seal it in the third ODI at Seddon Park, Hamilton, on Tuesday, November 10. For New Zealand, bowled out cheaply twice in two games, the batting has to improve quickly to keep the series alive. Full scores are in Cricbuzz's report.
